paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea: David swore he wouldn't rest until he found a place for the LORD, and the LORD answered with a promise of His own. The oath went one way, then it came right back the other way. David was thinking about a dwelling for God, and God was already thinking about David's throne, his people and his future (Psalm 132:2, 5, 11).

Now look at what the LORD promises, because it's BIG. He says, "One of your descendants I will place on your throne," and He calls it "a promise He will not revoke" (Psalm 132:11). There's an "if" for David's sons: if they keep His covenant, then their sons will also sit on the throne, so keeping the covenant matters (Psalm 132:12). And the LORD also says of Zion, "This is My resting place forever and ever" (Psalm 132:14). He holds both of those in the same song, friend, and I'm not going to smooth either one out.

So what does that mean for you, baker? The LORD sees the hard work, the sacrifice and the long nights, and He remembers (Psalm 132:1). He feeds the poor, He clothes His people with salvation, and He prepares a lamp for His anointed one (Psalm 132:15, 16, 17). Trust the One who keeps His promises, and take His words seriously too, because the crown upon His anointed one will gleam (Psalm 132:18).
